parole.significato: a foreigner who was not naturalised, and who had few rights
parole.testo: Uncertain. The TLF suggests a derivation from Frankish *alibanni (“a person belonging to another ban”). Another possible source is Latin *alibanus (“person from elsewhere”), from alibī (“elsewhere”).

Inherited from Middle French, Old French besoing; can be seen as a masculine variant of besogne, from Old French besonge, from Old Frankish *bisunnija, from *sunnijōn (“to look after”) (whence soigner), possibly through a Vulgar Latin intermediate *bisonium. Compare Italian bisogno.

From Frankish *tālōn (“to tear away, rip off”), via Latin, compare Spanish talar, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *tēlō (“persecution, deceit”). Cognate with Old High German zâlôn (“to root up, remove”), Old English tǣl (“reproof, calumny, mockery”).
